reuse.why: Holidays are folded into the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend via a new isNonWorkingDay helper that every path uses, but the daily-skip-versus-move dispatch is rewritten at each consumer rather than shared.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && daily ? drop non-working days : move via getDateWithSkippedWeekend' decision appears four times: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template's getEffectiveDate, each with its own lookahead bound (8+holidays, count*7+14, margin 3+holidays).

placement.why: isNonWorkingDay and the holiday-aware move rightly live in shared/schedules.ts, but occurrence adjustment logic is spread into server/schedules/app.ts and budget/schedule-template.ts.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; three release notes follow the repo convention.

maintainability.why: Any further change to how a schedule's effective occurrence is computed must be made in four places with different search bounds, and getEffectiveDate's re-call of getNextDate for daily schedules is subtle.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts and getEffectiveDate in budget/schedule-template.ts each re-decide the daily skip with isNonWorkingDay instead of a shared occurrence-adjustment function used by getNextDate

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip/move dispatch from getNextDate is reshaped as a bounded for-loop in getUpcomingDates, a Set-collecting range loop in getDatesInRange and a getNextDate re-call in getEffectiveDate

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a skipsWeekendDays special case with its own lookahead; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and getEffectiveDate (budget/schedule-template.ts) reimplement the daily-skip branch
